newsitem.title: USA: Allies found Nazi hoard of gold from human teeth.
newsitem.headline: Allies found Nazi hoard of gold from human teeth.

text.p: Allied soldiers found bags of gold fillings from human teeth in a Nazi cache in western Germany at the end of the Second World War, according to a previously secret U.S. army document.
The document, released on Wednesday by a Jewish group, said the Nazi cache of gold, jewels and cash was found by U.S. forces at the Kaiseroda salt mine at Merkers on April 8, 1945.

World Jewish Congress President Edgar Bronfman released it at a meeting of Jewish community leaders in which he gave an update on negotiations with Switzerland over return of assets from Holocaust victims that may still be in Swiss banks.

Jews are demanding the return of Holocaust victims' wealth ceded by Switzerland to Eastern European countries under controversial post-war accords to help compensate Swiss citizens for nationalized property.

The WJC has been combing the U.S. National Archives in a search for clues to the assets of Holocaust victims and to trace materials looted by the Nazis. The document, a report on what was found at the Kaiseroda salt mine, said the soldiers found containers holding "every conceivable kind of personal article of value and considerable currency."
Among the articles found were "Passover cups and candlestick holders, gold and silver dental work (full bags), watch chains and cases...."
Testimony at the Nuremberg War Crimes Tribunal said the Nazis extracted gold from the teeth of people they executed in death camps and melted it down to sell for their war effort.
Bronfman said he released the document to show that the looted Nazi gold his organization was trying to trace was not just gold bullion taken from the treasuries of Europe.
German soldiers used the Merkers salt mine to hide considerable amounts of gold and currency to keep it from falling into Russian hands at the end of the war.
